subject: Idea for a useful ggplot2 function

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Idea for a useful ggplot2 function
parts:
So I don't forget, it would be really useful to have a function say
match_layout, that given a list of ggplot2 graphics, returns a list of
the same number of graphics, but with the axes and legends sized
identically across all the graphics. It's similar to ggarrange, but
useful for the case where you want to lay out the graphics yourself.
I think this should be easy to do with gtable.

Hadley

--
Assistant Professor / Dobelman Family Junior Chair
Department of Statistics / Rice University

messages.author: affa918ed63b6275
messages.subject: Re: Idea for a useful ggplot2 function
parts:
I think it is possible by implementing interface for ggtable so that
each graphics will be returned separately.

gg <- ggtable(...)

gg_list <- get_each_panel_as_list(gg)

then, gglist is a list of gTree where all the figures have same width/height.
Now ggtable does not take care of legend though.

messages.subject: Re: Idea for a useful ggplot2 function

>
> I'm not sure putting them in a table would line them up correctly - I
> want both the vertical and horizontal elements to have the same sizes.

Yes exactly.
So the `get_each_panel_as_list` needs to do more things than simply
convert gtable to list.
It will align the row/col width/height of labels and axes, but not for panel.
Panel sizes are defined as "unit(1, 'null')" which means that a region
is divided equally.

kohske
